styles.label: Heritage
styles.blurb: Ruins of St. Paul's, A-Ma Temple and the UNESCO historic centre, all on foot.

styles.label: Macanese
styles.blurb: Portuguese-Chinese dishes, egg tarts and pork chop buns from old family kitchens.

styles.label: Casinos
styles.blurb: Big-name casino resorts, light shows and late-night bars on the Cotai Strip.

stays.why: Best base for the historic centre and Macanese restaurants. Most sights are a short walk away, and the buses are close by.
Near the ferry terminal for day trips to Hong Kong, Shenzhen and Zhuhai. Quieter, with a view over the water.
Old Portuguese streets, cafés and a relaxed village feel. Light rail and buses link it to the peninsula.
Large casino resorts with pools, shows and shops. Good for family stays and nightlife, but far from the old town on foot.

food: Try Macanese classics: African chicken, pork chop bun, minchi and Portuguese egg tarts.
Eat in old family-run restaurants in the historic centre and Taipa Village. Dishes are often shared.
Pork chop buns and egg tarts are cheap snacks. Buy them from bakeries and small cafés.
Casino resorts have many restaurants, from buffets to fine dining. Check opening hours before you go.
Booking ahead is wise for weekend dinners and popular Macanese restaurants. Check on the day.
more_time: Take a ferry from Outer Harbour for a day trip to Hong Kong. Check schedules and fares on the day.
Spend a half day in Coloane Village and the quiet beaches on the south side of the island.
Cross to Zhuhai for a day trip by ferry or land border. Check entry rules and visa needs before you go.

recommend.why: Two nights give you time for the historic centre, one day trip, and a casino resort evening without rushing.

month_notes: Jan: Cool at 14–19°C with 6 rain days. Good for walking the historic centre.
Feb: Cool at 15–20°C with 7 rain days. Pack a light jacket for evenings.
Mar: Mild at 18–23°C with 12 rain days. Showers are more frequent, so carry a compact umbrella.
Apr: Warm at 21–25°C with 14 rain days. Pleasant for outdoor sights between showers.
May: Hot at 25–28°C with 21 rain days. Humid, so plan indoor breaks in the afternoon.
Jun: Very hot at 27–30°C with 24 rain days. Expect frequent rain and heavy humidity.
Jul: Very hot at 27–31°C with 23 rain days. Start walking early and rest in the afternoon.
Aug: Hot at 27–30°C with 26 rain days. The wettest month, so keep plans flexible.
Sep: Hot at 26–30°C with 21 rain days. Check typhoon warnings before travel.
Oct: Pleasant at 23–27°C with 11 rain days. One of the best months for sightseeing.
Nov: Mild at 20–25°C with 7 rain days. Comfortable for walking and day trips.
Dec: Cool at 14–20°C with 4 rain days. Dry and good for sightseeing, with cool nights.

climate_guide.summary: Subtropical climate: hot, humid summers with heavy rain, and mild, drier winters.

items.title: Best time: October to December
items.text: Highs of about 23–27°C, with fewer rain days. Good for walking the historic centre.

items.title: Summer is hot and wet (June to September)
items.text: Highs of about 27–31°C, with 21–26 rain days a month. Plan indoor visits for the afternoon.

items.title: Humid most of the year
items.text: Humidity is high from May to September. Carry water and dress in light fabrics.

items.title: Rain is common in summer
items.text: Summer brings frequent showers. Bring a compact umbrella or light rain jacket.

items.title: Typhoon season
items.text: Typhoons are possible from about July to September. Check weather warnings and ferry status before travel.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light breathable clothes, sunscreen and a rain layer. Bring a warm layer for winter evenings.

transit.best: Walk the historic centre, then use buses with a Macau Pass card or taxis to cover longer distances.

modes.text: Macau has no metro system. Use the Light Rail or buses instead.
The Taipa Line links Taipa, Cotai and the Barra area. Check locally for current routes.
Buses cover the peninsula and islands. Pay with a Macau Pass card or exact cash coins. Check locally for fares.
Taxis are plentiful and cheap. Ask for the meter. Ride-hailing apps have limited availability, so check locally.
Driving is not recommended. Roads are congested and parking is scarce and costly.
The historic centre is best explored on foot. Taipa and Coloane suit cycling and shuttle buses.
Ferries run from Outer Harbour and Taipa to Hong Kong, Shenzhen and Zhuhai, so you can plan day trips by boat.
